subject: general
question: A dishonest shopkeeper pretends to sell his goods at cost price. However, he uses a false weight on which 984 gm is written, but actually weighs lesser. Using this false weight, the shopkeeper makes a gain of 23%. The actual measure of the weight used is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A **gain** of 23% implies that the ratio of **Actual weight** to **False weight** is 100 : 123.

Given **False weight** (Written weight) = 984 gm.

⇒ 123 units = 984 gm

⇒ 1 unit = 984 ÷ 123 = 8 gm

⇒ **Actual weight** = 100 units = 100 × 8 = 800 gm

**∴ The correct answer is 800gm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Written weight (True Value) = 984 gm

Gain percentage = 23%

**Formula Used:**

Gain % = [(Written Weight − Actual Weight) ÷ Actual Weight] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1ada29c0f3f945455b66293e0b513f3d58e707030f0a43c7782341aaa628b973.png] 

Let the **Actual weight** be x gm.

⇒ 23 = [(984 − x) ÷ x] × 100

⇒ 0.23x = 984 − x

⇒ x + 0.23x = 984

⇒ 1.23x = 984

⇒ x = 984 ÷ 1.23

⇒ x = 98400 ÷ 123

⇒ x = 800 gm

**∴ The correct answer is 800gm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer sells goods at **Cost Price** but uses a **false weight**, the profit percentage is calculated as: (Error ÷ Actual Weight) × 100.

Weight-Price Relation

The **Selling Price** is proportional to the **False weight** written on the scale, while the **Cost Price** is proportional to the **Actual weight** delivered.

Combined Profit

If a dealer also marks up the price by k% and uses a false weight, the **Overall Profit** is calculated by multiplying the respective ratios: (1 + k/100) × (True Weight ÷ Actual Weight).</p
